title: Investigation of Structural and Magnetic Properties of Mn3Ge Thin Film by Advanced Microscopy
content: The non-collinear antiferromagnet Mn3Ge has gained significant attention due to its exotic topological and magnetic properties, making it a promising candidate for next-generation spintronic applications. Its Kagome lattice structure gives rise to anomalous transport phenomena, including a large anomalous Hall effect (AHE) even in the absence of net magnetisation [1]. While bulk Mn3Ge has been extensively studied, its thin-film counterpart remains relatively unexplored. In particular, the relationship between crystallographic phase variations and ferromagnetic behaviour at the Mn3Ge interface requires further investigation. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) provides a high spatial resolution to examine the microstructure, composition, and phase-dependent magnetic properties of Mn3Ge thin films [2]. Furthermore, electron magnetic circular dichroism (EMCD) is employed to directly probe the element-specific magnetic moments of different phases [3-5], combining magnetic force microscopy (MFM) [6] and Lorentz differential phase contrast (LDPC) images provide new insights into their electronic and magnetic configurations.
